stage_a.note: The team smiles, uses upbeat tones, and enthusiastically presents the gift boxes to the panel.
Sal introduces Bouquet Bar with strong vocal energy and engaged, animated gestures.
The founders smile warmly and invite the sharks to help them bring gifting to everyone.

venture.description: An online gifting platform that allows customers to create custom gift boxes combining floral arrangements with premium treats.
venture.note: The primary industry is classified as other because gifting does not neatly fit the standard categories.

turns.speaker: F2
turns.summary: Sal introduces the team and states their ask of $150,000 for 10% of the company.

turns.speaker: S1
turns.summary: Kevin thanks them for the offer.

turns.speaker: F2
turns.summary: Sal notes that buying a gift for someone is not always easy.

turns.speaker: F3
turns.summary: Alex asks the panel to think about the last time they had to order a gift.

turns.speaker: F1
turns.summary: David asks if they were happy with the purchase or if they just bought a gift card.

turns.speaker: S2
turns.summary: Mark agrees.

turns.speaker: F2
turns.summary: Sal introduces Bouquet Bar as the perfect solution, combining flowers and unique gifts in amazing packaging.

turns.speaker: F1
turns.summary: David explains the process, starting with choosing a designer gift box.

turns.speaker: F2
turns.summary: Sal lists the gift options, including chocolates, tea blends, and beautifully arranged flowers.

turns.speaker: F3
turns.summary: Alex explains adding a custom note and finishing touches before sending the box.

turns.speaker: F2
turns.summary: Sal asks the sharks who wants to help them bring the art of gifting to everyone.

turns.speaker: S4
turns.summary: Daymond suggests they open the boxes and have some treats.

turns.speaker: S5
turns.summary: Lori agrees to open the boxes.

turns.speaker: S1
turns.summary: Kevin remarks that they like treats.

turns.speaker: S5
turns.summary: Lori asks Kevin to confirm they like treats.

turns.speaker: S1
turns.summary: Kevin jokes to Lori about treats causing weight gain.

turns.speaker: S5
turns.summary: Lori points out that Kevin only ever makes that joke to women.

turns.speaker: S2
turns.summary: Mark expresses surprise at what is inside his box.

turns.speaker: S5
turns.summary: Lori admires the smell and the beautiful, cute presentation.

turns.speaker: S1
turns.summary: Kevin agrees that the presentation is gorgeous.

turns.speaker: S2
turns.summary: Mark remarks that the box is nice.

turns.speaker: S5
turns.summary: Lori asks if the flowers in her box are a dozen roses.

turns.speaker: F1
turns.summary: David confirms that it is a dozen roses.

turns.speaker: S2
turns.summary: Mark asks how a customer mixes and matches items for the boxes.

turns.speaker: F2
turns.summary: Sal explains that customers select a box size on the site and then choose the corresponding number of items.

turns.speaker: S2
turns.summary: Mark asks how many different choices are available.

turns.speaker: F1
turns.summary: David bypasses the question by stating that they have only been out for four months.

turns.speaker: S3
turns.summary: The guest shark asks for confirmation that they have only been in business for four months.

turns.speaker: F1
turns.summary: David confirms four months and then answers Mark's earlier question, stating they have 22 SKUs and two bouquets.

turns.speaker: S2
turns.summary: Mark asks about shipping, noting that the box is heavy.

turns.speaker: S3
turns.summary: The guest shark interrupts to ask how much it costs to ship the heavy box.

turns.speaker: F1
turns.summary: David tells her it is okay and that they are ready for the numbers.

turns.speaker: S3
turns.summary: The guest shark repeats her question about the shipping cost due to the weight.

turns.speaker: F1
turns.summary: David answers that it currently costs twelve to fifteen dollars to ship the box.

turns.speaker: S4
turns.summary: Daymond asks for the average cost to make the small box with the product inside.

turns.speaker: F1
turns.summary: David states the small box costs about twenty dollars to make and sells for fifty dollars.

turns.speaker: F1
turns.summary: David adds that the second box costs thirty-four dollars to make and sells for seventy-five dollars.

turns.speaker: F1
turns.summary: David concludes that the last box costs sixty-eight dollars to make and sells for one hundred fifty-five dollars.

turns.speaker: S2
turns.summary: Mark asks the founders how they got into this business.

turns.speaker: F1
turns.summary: David explains that he and Alex have known each other for ten years and own a luxury floral design company.

turns.speaker: F3
turns.summary: Alex shares his background of being in the flower business for twenty-five years after immigrating from Iran.

turns.speaker: S3
turns.summary: The guest shark asks Alex how old he was when he came to the country.

turns.speaker: F3
turns.summary: Alex answers that he was fifteen and a half and worked at Burger King at night.

turns.speaker: F1
turns.summary: David shares his own immigrant story, describing how his dad sold pizzas and he sold flowers on the street.

turns.speaker: F1
turns.summary: David explains he studied biochemistry and wanted to be a doctor, but volunteering in an ER changed his mind.

turns.speaker: F1
turns.summary: David says they started Bouquet Bar two years ago and brought in his friend Sal to handle the technology side.

turns.speaker: F2
turns.summary: Sal explains his background in digital media and technology, and that he manages marketing and tech for the company.

turns.speaker: S2
turns.summary: Mark asks how much revenue their other floral design business generates.

turns.speaker: F1
turns.summary: David replies that the other business does about three million dollars annually.

turns.speaker: S1
turns.summary: Kevin asks if the investors would be getting a piece of that other business in this deal.

turns.speaker: F1
turns.summary: David clarifies that they are not asking for an investment in that other business.

turns.speaker: S1
turns.summary: Kevin dismissively remarks that that is what David says.

turns.speaker: S1
turns.summary: Kevin points out that customer acquisition cost is the main issue in the gifting business and asks how it works.

turns.speaker: F2
turns.summary: Sal states that their customer acquisition cost is about sixty dollars, utilizing online advertising channels.

turns.speaker: S1
turns.summary: Kevin immediately challenges that they are not making any money at all with that cost.

turns.speaker: F2
turns.summary: Sal defends the high cost by pointing out that they have just launched.

turns.speaker: S1
turns.summary: Kevin demands the sales numbers for the last four months.

turns.speaker: F1
turns.summary: David answers that they have done close to one hundred thousand dollars in sales.

turns.speaker: S4
turns.summary: Daymond asks how much of the founders' own money is invested in the business.

turns.speaker: F1
turns.summary: David answers that they have put in six hundred thousand dollars.

turns.speaker: S2
turns.summary: Mark asks if that figure includes external money or just their own.

turns.speaker: F1
turns.summary: David confirms it is entirely their own money.

turns.speaker: S3
turns.summary: The guest shark asks what the money was spent on.

turns.speaker: F1
turns.summary: David explains that half was spent on product development, process, operations, and a large facility with a cooler.

turns.speaker: F1
turns.summary: David adds they have three hundred thousand dollars in inventory, which translates to over a million in potential revenue.

turns.speaker: S1
turns.summary: Kevin brings the focus back to customer acquisition cost, insisting they need to lower it to ten to fifteen dollars.

turns.speaker: F2
turns.summary: Sal agrees with Kevin, conceding that is their goal but noting it will take time to achieve.

turns.speaker: S2
turns.summary: Mark asks who their target customer is.

turns.speaker: F2
turns.summary: Sal states their current customers are males and females between thirty-five and fifty-five, predominantly female.

turns.speaker: F1
turns.summary: David adds that they are going to teach people how to gift, as many are scared to do so.

turns.speaker: S5
turns.summary: Lori points out that the product looks just like the packaging from Sugarfina.

turns.speaker: F1
turns.summary: David asks what Sugarfina is, admitting he does not know the competitor.

turns.speaker: S5
turns.summary: Lori explains that Sugarfina fills boxes like theirs with different candies as their trademark.

turns.speaker: F1
turns.summary: David dismisses the comparison by stating that Sugarfina is just a candy company.

turns.speaker: S5
turns.summary: Lori argues that customers searching online will find Sugarfina, which is less expensive.

turns.speaker: S5
turns.summary: Lori advises them to leverage their floral expertise to be more unique and beat the competitor.

turns.speaker: F3
turns.summary: Alex acknowledges the candy similarity but notes he is designing other new items for future lines.

turns.speaker: S5
turns.summary: Lori states she would have been interested if they had presented more innovative floral designs at a great price.

turns.speaker: S5
turns.summary: Lori exits, citing that despite their drive, they have not figured the business out yet.

turns.speaker: S3
turns.summary: The guest shark agrees with Lori about the Sugarfina similarity and thinks their difference is easy to replicate.

turns.speaker: S3
turns.summary: The guest shark exits because the point of differentiation is not large enough for her.

turns.speaker: S4
turns.summary: Daymond argues that educating people who do not know how to gift will be very hard.

turns.speaker: F1
turns.summary: David jokes about losing a girlfriend.

turns.speaker: S4
turns.summary: Daymond continues that customer education will be difficult and cost a lot of money.

turns.speaker: S4
turns.summary: Daymond exits because the cost of educating customers will be too high.

turns.speaker: F1
turns.summary: David counters the negativity by pointing to other large markets, such as the billion-dollar wedding market.

turns.speaker: S1
turns.summary: Kevin corrects the market size figure to three billion.

turns.speaker: S1
turns.summary: Kevin praises the quality but reiterates that he prefers to invest where customer acquisition is already solved.

turns.speaker: S1
turns.summary: Kevin exits with a heavy heart because the customer acquisition problem remains unsolved.

turns.speaker: S2
turns.summary: Mark jokes that the riff-raff is out of the way.

turns.speaker: S2
turns.summary: Mark asks if their corporate gift selling relies on salespeople or just walk-in business.

turns.speaker: F1
turns.summary: David answers that it is all done by salespeople.

turns.speaker: S2
turns.summary: Mark asks if those salespeople can work purely on commission.

turns.speaker: F1
turns.summary: David confirms that they can.

turns.speaker: S2
turns.summary: Mark asks how flexible they are to create different designs, implying they rely too much on flowers.

turns.speaker: F1
turns.summary: David states they are innovative and he would love to design more items.

turns.speaker: S2
turns.summary: Mark asserts that the 10% equity offer is not enough and asks why they thought it was.

turns.speaker: F1
turns.summary: David defends the ask, stating the 1.5 million dollar valuation is not that high.

turns.speaker: F1
turns.summary: David adds that their creation required the integration of multiple companies' capabilities.

turns.speaker: S2
turns.summary: Mark points out that they will inevitably need more money.

turns.speaker: F1
turns.summary: David begins to reply but is cut off by Mark.

turns.speaker: S2
turns.summary: Mark asks specifically what they will need more money for and when.

turns.speaker: F1
turns.summary: David replies that the capital would be used for sales, operations, and staffing.

turns.speaker: S2
turns.summary: Mark argues that an e-commerce company should virtualize operations and not need a large staff.

turns.speaker: S2
turns.summary: Mark repeats his question about why they need to spend a lot more money.

turns.speaker: F1
turns.summary: David attempts to answer but is interrupted again.

turns.speaker: S2
turns.summary: Mark asks if the need for money is because their funds are tied up in inventory.

turns.speaker: F1
turns.summary: David denies this, stating they have inventory and are fully ready to sell right now.

turns.speaker: S2
turns.summary: Mark insists they must give up more equity or they will not secure a deal.

turns.speaker: S2
turns.summary: Mark adds that they are going to have to spend significantly more money.

turns.speaker: F1
turns.summary: David counters that they have one hundred thousand in the bank and he is willing to refinance his house if needed.

turns.speaker: S2
turns.summary: Mark acknowledges this but tries to return to his point.

turns.speaker: F1
turns.summary: David reiterates their readiness, explaining that adding new products will not be expensive to ship.

turns.speaker: F1
turns.summary: David emphasizes that they are ready and have the necessary salespeople in place.

turns.speaker: S2
turns.summary: Mark offers them one hundred fifty thousand dollars for twenty percent equity, stating it is non-negotiable.

turns.speaker: S3
turns.summary: The guest shark prompts the founders for an answer to Mark's offer.

turns.speaker: F1
turns.summary: David accepts Mark's offer on behalf of the team.

decisions.note: Lori exits because she feels they haven't figured the business out yet and lack sufficient differentiation.
The guest shark exits because the point of differentiation from competitors is not big enough.
Daymond exits because educating customers how to gift will be very hard and expensive.
Kevin exits because he prefers to invest where customer acquisition is an already solved problem.
Mark offers $150k for 20% because he believes they will need to spend more money to grow.
David accepts Mark's non-negotiable offer on behalf of the founders.

record.notes: S3 is a guest shark wearing a pink dress; her name is not clearly spoken during the pitch, so she is labeled Pink Dress Shark. S5 is Lori Greiner.
